title: ‘Phantom’ Data Centers Are Demanding More From the Power Grid Than They Need
source_used: Breitbart News (relaying the Wall Street Journal)
key_facts: The Wall Street Journal reports that AI's electricity appetite has buried utilities in requests for grid connections, many of which will never become real buildings; the industry calls them 'phantom' data centers.
Utilities are tightening rules for new AI data center customers, requiring binding financial commitments, collateral and steep engineering fees.
Wood Mackenzie, a research firm, puts only 23 percent of disclosed data-center requests in the 'high confidence' category.

Exelon, a utility operating across the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, says typical requests used to be about 50 megawatts and now reach 1,000 megawatts or more; its large-customer requests tripled to 18,000 megawatts.
After Exelon required binding commitments and collateral, its high-probability list fell from 18,000 to 11,000 megawatts, with the remaining projects posting roughly $1 billion in collateral.
Average minimum contract lengths for large customers have grown to about 10.8 years since 2024, from about 4.6 years before, per utility filings aggregated by the AI startup Halcyon.
Texas now requires large customers to pay a $50,000-per-megawatt deposit for engineering studies, so a 500-megawatt data center owes $25 million upfront.

why_it_matters_hint: Utilities want proof that data centers are real before building grid capacity that other customers might end up paying for.
